decisions.basis: The CHM oral history printed p.17 has Kattner retrospectively recall an end-1960 decision to phase out physically isolated Phase Two; Last simultaneously recalled a December 1960 memo still weighing physical versus junction isolation. This is an attributed decision, not a date of completed cessation; the node decline stays unknown.

The Finnish museum collection account states that IBM 305 production ceased in 1961, market withdrawal came in 1969, and a particular OTK machine was used in Helsinki during the 1960s. The type description names the 350 disk but not a serial; retrospective market and production endpoints do not prove last use. No exact first or last OTK operating date is inferred.

The March 1961 BRL survey printed p.393 lists Douglas Tulsa standard IBM 701 equipment and an additional 726 tape unit for $850 per month. The system customer-acceptance date does not independently date the third unit or show a particular tape operation. The retained excerpt is pixel-identical to original segment PDF p.94 at 60 dpi.

NRC RFC 942 printed pp.25–26 explicitly dates the NCP-to-TCP cutover to 1 January 1983 and says operational capability continued during transition, without proving every individual host converted that day. CHM dates formal ARPANET shutdown to 1990, consistent with DARPA prose; the latter agency page also says 1989 in its evolution timeline. Original ARPANET closure is not the end of the wider Internet, MILNET or host activity.
